about: Laws that have no researched outcome-web link in data/research/outcome-web/links.json, neither from the law itself nor from a measure an engine sets from it, and the outcome the research would measure. Each carries the stopgap that registers the gap; read by scripts/law-wiring/catalog.ts for the law-wiring matrix. The research belongs to the outcome-web line (pool item laws-outcome-links-unresearched). A row's note records a search that found no sized source.

laws.note: Searched again Oct 25, 2026 (claude, laws-outcome-links-rest); no study sizes what a state or local natural resources line does to a measure the web keeps, so no link is built and the row stays. What the line is: the Census Bureau's natural resources spending is "conservation and management of resources, such as fish and game, forestry, soil, water, and electric energy resources" (Census Bureau, Public spending on protecting environment up, June 2021, https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2021/06/public-spending-on-protecting-environment-up.html); parks are a separate line, already linked (parks-spending-to-exercise-access). Searched: (1) state park funding and visitation: Smith, Wilkins and Leung 2019 (PNAS 116, doi 10.1073/pnas.1902314116, abstract read through Europe PMC) find that "Attendance is the single largest factor affecting the operations of America's state park systems", the reverse direction (visits drive spending), and no study of funding driving visits turned up. (2) Conservation spending and land protected: Larson 2025 (Virginia conservation easements, https://www.montana.edu/econ/klarson/Larsoneasements.pdf) finds an acreage elasticity of -1.13 to -1.47 to the post-tax price of donating an easement, and cites Parker and Thurman 2018 at -2.4 to -6.1; these answer a tax subsidy on private donations, not a budget line. (3) Farmland preservation: Liu and Lynch 2007 (https://farmlandinfo.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2019/09/Do_Agricultural_Preservation_Programs_Affect_Farmland_Conversion_-_liu_and_lynch5_1.pdf) find that having a purchase-of-development-rights program "decrease[s] the rate of farmland loss by 2.2 to 3.1 percentage points", a comparison of counties with and without a program, not of spending levels, and the web already links the law on protecting farmland (farmland-easements-to-farmland-lost). (4) Land and Water Conservation Fund grants and park visits: program reports only, no causal estimate. Neither land protected nor park visits is a measure the web keeps. Next step: a sized study of natural resources or park operating spending on a count the web can keep (visits, protected acres).
